problems.title: Two Sum
problems.description: Given an array of integers nums and an integer target, return indices of the two numbers such that they add up to target. You may assume each input has exactly one solution and you may not use the same element twice.

bruteForce.explanation: Check every pair of elements to see if they sum to target. Two nested loops iterate over all combinations.

optimal.explanation: Use an unordered_map to store each number and its index. For each number, check if its complement (target - num) already exists in the map — giving O(1) lookup instead of a full scan.

problems.title: Valid Parentheses
problems.description: Given a string s containing just the characters '(', ')', '{', '}', '[' and ']', determine if the input string is valid. Open brackets must be closed by the same type of brackets in the correct order.

bruteForce.explanation: Repeatedly find and remove matched pairs () [] {} from the string until no more are found, then check if the result is empty.

optimal.explanation: Use a stack. Push opening brackets. For each closing bracket, check if the stack top is the matching opening — if so pop, otherwise return false.

problems.title: Maximum Subarray
problems.description: Given an integer array nums, find the subarray with the largest sum and return its sum.

bruteForce.explanation: Try all possible subarrays using two nested loops. For each starting index, accumulate the sum and track the maximum found.

optimal.explanation: Kadane's Algorithm: at each position decide whether to extend the running sum or start fresh. currentSum = max(num, currentSum + num). Track the global max throughout.

problems.title: Binary Search
problems.description: Given a sorted array of integers and a target value, return the index of the target if found, otherwise return -1.

bruteForce.explanation: Linear search: iterate through every element and compare with the target.

optimal.explanation: Binary search: maintain left/right pointers. At each step check the midpoint — if target found return it; if mid < target move left right; if mid > target move right left.

problems.title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
problems.description: Given a string s, find the length of the longest substring without duplicate characters.

bruteForce.explanation: Try all substrings starting from each index. For each, track characters in a set and stop when a duplicate is encountered.

optimal.explanation: Sliding window with a hash map storing last seen index. When a duplicate is found, jump the left pointer past the previous occurrence instead of starting over.

problems.title: Climbing Stairs
problems.description: You are climbing a staircase with n steps. Each time you can either climb 1 or 2 steps. In how many distinct ways can you climb to the top?

bruteForce.explanation: Recursive approach: total ways = ways(n-1) + ways(n-2). Exponential time due to overlapping subproblems.

optimal.explanation: This is the Fibonacci sequence. Track only the previous two values and compute iteratively — no recursion, no extra array needed.

problems.title: Reverse Linked List
problems.description: Given the head of a singly linked list, reverse the list and return the reversed list.

bruteForce.explanation: Collect all node values into a vector, reverse it, then rebuild the linked list from scratch.

optimal.explanation: Iterate through the list reversing each node's next pointer in-place using prev and curr pointers. No extra space needed.

problems.title: Contains Duplicate
problems.description: Given an integer array nums, return true if any value appears at least twice, and false if every element is distinct.

bruteForce.explanation: Compare every pair of elements using nested loops. If any two are equal, return true.

optimal.explanation: Use an unordered_set. As we iterate, if the current element is already in the set return true, otherwise insert it.
